Library
Full Backup & Restore
Works even if the API is egress-blocked
This pulls data through the same connection the live app already uses. If that connection is blocked (egress cap, paused project), this tool will be blocked too — in that case, use SQL Editor Mode below, which never touches that layer.
Download Backup
Pulls every table from the currently connected project and saves it as one JSON file to your device.
Restore Backup
Loads a previously downloaded backup file into the currently connected project. Existing rows are never overwritten — new rows are added and matching IDs are skipped.
Auto-Backup Reminder
Shows a reminder on this device if it's been more than 7 days since your last backup. Doesn't run automatically in the background — you still tap the button — but you won't forget.
Verify a Backup File
Checks row counts and structure without restoring anything — useful right after downloading, to confirm the file isn't truncated or corrupted.
When to use this
Supabase blocks the app's REST connection when a project hits its egress cap or is paused — but the SQL Editor in the Supabase dashboard talks to Postgres directly and is not affected by that block.

If "Download Full Backup" above fails with a network or 401 error, this is the reliable fallback:
  1. Open your Supabase dashboard for the affected project
  2. Go to SQL Editor
  3. Run the export query below (generates INSERT statements for every table)
  4. Copy the result and save it as a .sql file
  5. To restore: paste that file's contents into the SQL Editor of the destination project and run it
Export query

Preview Ads as Regular User
Owners are always ad-free by default — flip this on to actually see ads render in the feed/channels while testing, on this device only.
"Post" ads look like a real post (image + text) and appear roughly once every 10 posts in the Home feed, at a random spot within each 10. "Card" ads are compact and appear at the top of every channel's broadcast list — best for promoting in-app features like Premium. Premium subscribers never see either.
